sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "The key thing is that there is help out there, it's just tapping into it." How sleep tracking can make your sleep worse The hidden cost of the night shift and how to sleep it off

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Dr Javed Hussain performs a range of cosmetic procedures, including penis fillers Dr Javed Hussain has been offering penis fillers for more than a year at his clinic in Prestwich, Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hussain trained as a doctor before moving into cosmetic procedures, but penis fillers do not legally require any medical training to perform.

sentences.text: He says demand is increasing.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The hyaluronic acid filler is delivered through a cannula that enters at the base and travels along the length of the shaft.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: If you see someone you think has heat exhaustion , the NHS says you should: , external move them to a cool place get them to lie down and raise their feet slightly get them to drink plenty of water - sports or rehydration drinks are also OK cool their skin - spray or sponge them with cool water and fan them.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Cold packs around the armpits or neck are also good If they can be cooled down within half an hour, then heat exhaustion is not normally serious.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, if they do not recover within 30 minutes, then they are at risk of heatstroke .
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This is a medical emergency and you should call 999 immediately.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People with heatstroke may stop sweating even though they are too hot.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Their temperature could go over 40C and they might have seizures or lose consciousness.

sentences.text: What to do if you think someone has heat exhaustion or heatstroke People who are older or have some long-term conditions - such as heart disease -  are sometimes less able to cope with the strain heat puts on the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diabetes can make the body lose water more quickly and some complications of the disease can alter blood vessels and the ability to sweat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Children and those who are less mobile may also be more vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Brain diseases, such as dementia, can also leave people unaware of the heat or unable to do anything about it.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People who are homeless will also be more exposed to the sun.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Those living in top-floor flats will also face higher temperatures.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Yes - but the NHS says people should keep taking their medication as normal, and focus on staying cool and hydrated.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diuretics - sometimes called "water pills" - increase the amount of water the body expels.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: They are taken widely, including for heart failure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: In high temperatures, they increase the dangers of dehydration and imbalances in key minerals in the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Antihypertensives - which lower blood pressure - can combine with the blood vessels that are dilating to cope with the heat and cause dangerous drops in blood pressure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Some drugs for people with epilepsy and Parkinson's can block sweating and make it harder for the body to cool itself.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Other drugs such as lithium or statins can become more concentrated and problematic in the blood if there is too much fluid loss.

sentences.text: During 2022 - which saw the highest recorded temperature in England at 40.3C - there were an estimated 2,985 so-called "excess deaths" as a result of the heat , external , the most recorded in any given year.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: There were an estimated 1,311 heat-associated deaths , external during summer 2024, and an estimated 1,504 , external during summer 2025.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Most heat-related excess deaths are due to heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The higher death rate starts to kick in once the thermometer passes 25C-26C.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, evidence suggests the deaths tend to be caused by higher temperatures in spring or early summer rather than during "peak summer".
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This could be because we start to change our day-to-day behaviour as summer progresses and we get more used to dealing with the heat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The evidence from previous heatwaves is the increase in deaths happens very quickly - within the first 24 hours of a heatwave.

sentences.text: Cami Sophia sees September as a chance to get ahead with her goals The lazy hazy days of summer may feel like a distant memory as September shifts our energy back to business and forward to new adventures.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: It's the month when many of us embark on a new chapter, whether it's university, college or a new job or simply getting back to work and the school run.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: It's also the time that "September Reset" trends on social media - the kind, chill sister of New Year's Resolutions.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Instead of strict rules and major life overhauls, creators are sharing small changes aimed at finishing the year strong.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "It's getting ahead of the game," says Cami Sophia, 24, who has shared her new rituals on TikTok.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Here's why September could be the right time for a reset and how to create a new routine that lasts.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Should you get back into a routine?
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: For Cami, a content creator and podcast host from Northampton, September spells the end of summer spontaneity and a time to restore order.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "If you've been away for the summer you've probably not had a massive routine," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "And if you're a parent, then you've got kids at home and it's just a bit more chaotic," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: September feels like "back to school...getting back into your own rhythm", she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: It is the perfect time to "get everything sorted", she says "So when you get to January you're not trying to do everything at once.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: For Bas Verplanken, professor emeritus of social psychology at the University of Bath, September is a chance to "reorient yourself".
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: He says his research suggests people who experienced a big change such as moving house "were more responsive to an intervention aimed at promoting sustainable behaviours" than comparable people who had not moved house.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "It's really an exciting way of looking at disruption," he told Chris and Xand van Tulleken on their What's Up Docs? podcast.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: If your daily commute or school run works for you then relax back into them.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "But if there are alternative ways of doing things, explore it, this is the time to do it, and to make those changes," says Verplanken.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Cami preps meals and books workout classes in advance to stick to her routine TikTok is awash with videos on how to "lock in" starting small - declutter your room, clear out your wardrobe, go for a walk, start a new book.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: But Cami warns against videos showing spreadsheets of radical changes.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "It's very easy to look at all of these things and what you should apparently be doing and get really overwhelmed," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Cami starts her own reset by "looking at the goals I set at the start of the year and see what I actually still want to do - and then what I need to do to get from A to B".
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Then she recommends picking three small "non-negotiables".
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "They could be to have fruit with your breakfast, have veg with dinner and have a glass of water before you drink coffee," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: She advises small changes that require little effort - she is getting back into sleep patterns by setting alarms.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Drs Chris and Xand van Tulleken are on a mission to help us take better care of ourselves.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Listen to What's Up Docs? on BBC Sounds or wherever you get your BBC podcasts." Cami says planning is key - something she does on a Sunday morning.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "I go, okay, these are my meals for the week.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: These are my workouts for the week.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Even plan your outfits for the work day if you really want to because it saves you time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Then she takes steps to "limit the choices" she has to stray from her routine.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "I will meal prep three days worth of overnight oats.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Naturally, I'm going to grab those in the morning because they are made and ready.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: I've removed the friction of grabbing a quick meal or not having any breakfast." Verplanken agrees the secret to making new habits that last is setting yourself up so that your new behaviours are the easiest option for reaching your goal.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: He advises designing a routine where your habits can become "effortless".
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "They are specific plans of where, when, and what you will do," he says.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: "Let's say, losing weight, you can think when I go to the supermarket, I'm going to look specifically each time [at] the fat and sugar content [of food].
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: It's a very specific plan." This means making the right choices when are facing the food shelf happen automatically "because you have already planned the situation in which you have to act".
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: If this is done frequently, Verplanken says it becomes "extremely effective" to turn these habits into your routine.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: Carys Louise Brandon says she was completely unprepared for what came after her first C-section Mothers have described being left to recover from caesarean sections with "no support" as the number of babies being born via caesarean reaches its highest rate on record.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: A caesarean, or C-section, is a major operation to deliver a baby through a cut in the abdomen, usually just below the bikini line.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Carys Louise Brandon, from Swansea, had an emergency C-section to deliver her first child in 2022 and said she was completely unprepared for what came afterwards.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: The Welsh government said every woman should receive high-quality postnatal care tailored to her needs.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Carys Louise says she had many unanswered questions about her recovery Latest figures show 42% of babies in Wales were born by C-section in 2025, with just over half of those operations being emergencies.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Carys' first baby was born in 2022.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: After needing an emergency C-section, Carys, a content creator, said she had many unanswered questions about her recovery.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "I think I was thrown in at the deep end and I really didn't know how to deal with it," she said.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: It was almost three weeks before the 29-year-old said she felt physically able to leave the house.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "And even then, I only walked up to the top of the street and back," she added.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Carys has since had two more caesareans and said each experience was very different.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Both times, she said the care she received in hospital and from her community midwife was good.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: But after getting home, she was left with questions about how her body should be recovering.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "You're thrown so into the deep end and there's no sort of, 'Oh, this is how your scar should look.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: This is quite normal for this sort of time'." She recalled taking the dressing off her wound and fainting in the shower.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "I didn't know - should my scar be recovering in a certain way, should I really be feeling like this?
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "There's just no support around the fact that after it, you're looking after a baby and recovering from major surgery, and everyone's recovery looks totally different." She has shared her own experiences online in the hopes of helping other women, and said expectant mums often contact her for advice.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: According to the NHS , external , a caesarean may be recommended as a planned procedure or carried out in an emergency if a vaginal birth is considered to be too risky.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Some women also choose to have a caesarean for non-medical reasons.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: The health service's website states that most women can go home from hospital one or two days after a C-section, but that recovery is normally slower than from a vaginal birth.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: A Welsh government report published in February highlighted the rapid increase in caesarean sections and inductions, saying the consequences for women, their families and the NHS had not been evaluated.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: The report raised concerns about staffing and support across maternity services and said postnatal care was inadequately staffed and supported.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: The Welsh government has committed to a three-year programme of improvements, but the Royal College of Midwives (RCM) said maternity services had not kept pace with the changing picture.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: New mums 'left to get on with it' after C-sections Julie Richards, director of the RCM in Wales, said postnatal care for C-sections should include support with pain relief, wound care and surgical recovery, alongside help with feeding and caring for a new baby.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: She said the rise in caesareans had changed the demands being placed on services.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Ceri Ann had an emergency C-section and her daughter, Ania, was taken to neonatal intensive care because she was not breathing.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Ceri Ann said she was then left alone on the recovery ward, unable to move.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "I just wanted to see my baby but I couldn't, and the staff told me there was no-one available to take me up to see her." She said it was seven hours until she held her baby for the first time, and that was when her husband arrived back at the hospital and took her to the unit himself.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "It was awful, I just cried and cried," she said.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: It acknowledged that being separated from a baby following birth could be distressing and said its teams worked to facilitate contact "at the earliest safe opportunity".
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Nicola Rous-Morgan is a pregnancy and postnatal yoga teacher, and a trained midwife who works with women recovering after childbirth Nicola Rous-Morgan is a pregnancy and postnatal yoga teacher and a trained midwife, who works with women recovering after childbirth, including those who have had C-sections.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: She said women often tell her they feel left alone to manage their recovery by themselves.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "I think one of the biggest take-homes is they felt that once they had been discharged from hospital, upon coming home, that they were just left to get on with it." She added: "The focus is on women who are recovering from vaginal delivery.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: It's not geared towards women who are recovering from major abdominal surgery." Nicola said women should not have to rely on private services or social media to find basic recovery information.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "These things shouldn't be things that women have to pay for privately.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: What happens to the women that can't afford that luxury?" The RCM said staffing pressures were one factor affecting the care available.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Richards said: "Our midwives are stretched, and quite often that is often impacted into the postnatal care, into the community settings." The RCM surveyed its members in Wales in July, and 94% of respondents said they were not able to give the care they would like to give.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: The organisation said midwives were working extra shifts and being moved to cover shortages elsewhere in maternity services.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Richards said more investment and a workforce plan was needed.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: The Welsh government said every woman should receive high-quality postnatal care tailored to their needs.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: A spokesperson added: "Maternity teams provide postnatal assessment, advice and support following birth, and where required, women can be referred to specialist services including obstetric physiotherapy.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "Referrals are determined by individual clinical need to ensure women receive the most appropriate care to support their recovery and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston trains for her powerlifting competitions at a gym in Redditch A teenage powerlifter managed to win double golds at a world championship despite her endometriosis flaring up to leave her in excruciating pain just before the competition.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston, from Redditch, also landed second on the podium with a silver and a bronze medal, across three events in the World Sub-Junior & Junior Powerlifting Championships, in South Africa last month.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: The 18-year-old only took up the sport three years ago, after being inspired by her brother to give it a go.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Weston now uses social media to speak openly about having endometriosis and being a young woman in the sport of powerlifting, in the hope of empowering others.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston placed second overall at the World Sub-Junior & Junior Powerlifting Championships Lhamo told the BBC she loves competing in the sport because of its inclusivity.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "I love how inclusive it is and how we're like a community," she said.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "Everyone knows each other and are really supportive of each other, and I just think it's an amazing sport that really brings people together." She stood on the podium in the Under 57kg category at the championship after getting two golds in squat and deadlift, and a bronze in the bench event.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "It felt incredible to be completely honest, I went into it with expectations of potentially reaching podium.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: I didn't initially expect to place second or even have a chance at placing first," she said.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "It can affect my training with the pain, I get quite tired and I also get back pain which can feel the same as a back injury.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: It was difficult but we managed to do it." Lhamo has been celebrating back home with her medals Endometriosis affects one in 10 women in the UK, but she says many people don't know about it.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "There's not enough awareness about it and how it actually impacts women and girls," she continued.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "I've been dealing with endometriosis since I was 12, and I only got diagnosed last year.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: It was a very long journey and I just think there needs to be more awareness so we can try and find solutions to help other people.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "As for powerlifting, if you want to do it, go for it.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: At the end of the day, there's nothing holding you back." Sam Pope from Elite Fitness in Redditch says Lhamo is an inspiration to all The teenager trains at Elite Fitness gym in Redditch and, despite recently moving to Worcester, still travels the 45 minutes to get there.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Sam Pope, who works there, says Lhamo is an inspiration.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "For other young people of her age, it just shows that actually if you put the effort in, the reward is there," he said.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.

sentences.text: Although the UK performed well overall, the rankings varied significantly again, with results showing England, where the curriculum is significantly different, pulling consistently ahead of Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: One father, Gerry, said years of disagreements with the CMS had pushed him to the brink - including after it added an extra child, who was not his, to his account.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: Gerry was among more than 1,000 parents who contacted BBC Your Voice about the CMS earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: He has two children from separate relationships.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: His salary has fluctuated with different jobs, and he has been a student, but the CMS has often struggled to keep up, he told us.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "I contacted them to say I can't deal with this stress.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: It's causing me anxiety [and] depression," he said.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: A decade ago, Gerry queried arrears on his account with the CMS.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: It investigated, but in doing so, created a much bigger problem.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: It added a third child to his account, though he only had two children he was required to pay for.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: Once Gerry noticed this mistake, he became "numb".
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: The CMS paid him a £100 "consolatory payment" and an internal note said mistakes at the time had caused Gerry "gross inconvenience".
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: But he said he then faced more problems - being liable for child maintenance for about 18 months longer than necessary for his older child.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: In October last year, he took the CMS to a tribunal and won.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: However, his initial relief disappeared when the CMS told him, because he had paid the mother directly, he would have to ask her for the refund himself.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: What is more, the bill for his monthly payments then almost trebled to £981 a month, after it appeared he had now underpaid for the younger child still entitled to support.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: The CMS system had added the outstanding amount, and some arrears he had been disputing, to his continuing payments to come up with the new figure.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "I'm instantly broke, panic attack, phoning GPs, back on medication, anxiety through the roof," Gerry said.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: Marion Fellows raised Gerry's case in Parliament Marion Fellows, who was Gerry's MP for nine years until 2024, raised his case in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "I think Gerry's case is atrocious," she told Panorama.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "What CMS have done to Gerry over the years is not right.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: But it's not, it's CMS." The CMS said it had acknowledged and apologised for previous failings in Gerry's case and made consolatory payments.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: It said it had given him explanations and assurances on action taken and ongoing payments.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: Concerns about the CMS were raised with government in a House of Lords report entitled Reforming the Child Maintenance Service, in October 2025.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: One parent described enforcement as "random, abusive and unregulated".
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "It punishes the wrong people and ignores real avoidance," the report stated.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: The government is planning to reform the CMS by moving all parents on to Collect and Pay and reducing the fees it charges.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: The DWP said it would "improve compliance" and "deliver better outcomes for children".
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: CMS director Simon Hunter told Panorama he believed the service "has worked pretty effectively".
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "Every case has its own set of circumstances and there are always two sides to the case as well so… we do work through that as best as we possibly can," he said.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "Any opportunity for us, for myself, to improve the service, then we will absolutely take that on board." To parents who have been affected by "administrative mistakes... where we have made life difficult for our customers - I absolutely apologise for that", he added.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: Lots of parents successfully use the CMS, but when the system fails the consequences can be huge for parents and children.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "It can't go on," Gerry said.
sentences.article_title: Parents pushed to breaking point by Child Maintenance Service, BBC told

sentences.text: "It's too many lives being broken." Additional reporting by Tammi Walker Are you affected by the issues raised in this story?

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The Lib Dems say schools are approaching an "existential crisis" in teacher retention Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Lib Dem proposals include the government fully funding teacher's pay, which will increase in England by 3.5% from September, with an additional 3% the year after.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Currently, half of the pay increase will come from existing school budgets.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The party is also calling for proper enforcement of teacher's legally mandated working hours, the introduction of reasonable limits on overtime, and for all schools to be required to introduce flexible working policies.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The party did not identify where funding might come from to pay for the policies.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: An education department spokesperson said: "We know teachers do an incredible job and we're determined to make sure that dedication is matched with the right support.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "Last year saw one of the lowest rates of teachers leaving the profession since 2010, and a record number of teachers returning to the classroom, but we know there's more to do.

sentences.text: Friends Amelia (left) and Beatrice (right) are living at home when they start university this September More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In 2017, it was closer to one in five.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Students told the BBC the rising cost of living was a major influence in deciding what to do after school or college.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For friends Beatrice and Amelia, who are from St Helens, Merseyside, the cost of accommodation was a big factor in their decision to live at home while studying.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Both are heading to university in September, but neither will be moving into student accommodation.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Beatrice is going to the University of Manchester to study maths and plans to commute by train, a journey which can take about 50 minutes in total.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "My first choice was Manchester and then my second was Liverpool, so I knew I could commute," she says, adding that the price of accommodation would have been "a few grand a year".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Amelia, who is going to study at Liverpool John Moores University - approximately 20 minutes away by train - says the accommodation she found was between £300 and £400 a week.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Although neither is looking forward to the commute, both are still hoping they can get the full experience of university while living at home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: My three-hour university commute is worth the £7,000 saving on halls However, fellow student Jessica, who is also going to study at Liverpool John Moores University, feels she will miss out.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: She says she would have loved to live on campus and enjoy student life, but the price of renting is "ridiculous" and "insane".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "I have a part-time job as everything is so expensive, and then commuting is going to kill a lot of my free time as well," she says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "It is a bit sad really when you think about it." But she is pleased that staying at home means she will still be able to have her mum and dad's cooked dinners.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Earlier this year, BBC News followed the daily journey of one first-year student who said she was saving over £7,000 on accommodation by commuting 90 minutes into Manchester each day from home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures were recorded on results day and are expected to rise over the coming month as more students accept university places through clearing.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: A record number of UK 18-year-olds have been accepted into university this year.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: But student rents have risen sharply in recent years, alongside other living costs.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The Higher Education Policy Institute (Hepi) said last year that students needed £61,000 over the course of a three-year degree in order to have a "minimum socially acceptable standard of living" - and that's excluding tuition fees.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Its report found that in 2024 the cost of renting in university-owned accommodation ranged from £108 per week, for 40 to 44-week contracts in Northern Ireland, to £338 a week for the shortest contracts in London, where rent makes up nearly half (46%) of students' costs.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In most areas it was between £140 and £180 a week, with private halls usually being more expensive.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Many students are eligible for a maintenance loan, which can help with the cost of accommodation, but the average annual price of a room on campus is increasing much faster, according to some student unions .

sentences.text: Hepi says most young full-time students now work in paid employment during term time to make up the difference between their maintenance loan income and the cost of living.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For some students, it means a rethink about what university looks like.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs
