sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Almost 3,400 18-and 19-year-olds joined the university last year – making up 9.5% of new starters, compared with 5.7% six years ago.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Traditionally, it has been popular with mature students wanting to continue working while studying from home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Its vice-chancellor, Prof Dave Phoenix, says it points to a shift in how younger people are thinking about university, adding that studying online "means they can avoid moving costs and high accommodation bills and, for others, it means keeping a job".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: But a recent report , external by Prof William Whyte, from the University of Oxford, argues that the value of on-campus life extends far beyond the price of accommodation, and plays an important role in personal development and the wider university experience.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "The question isn't simply where students live.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: It's what they gain from living and learning together as part of a university community," he says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: When I attended pregnancy scans a decade ago, the best the sonographer could do to involve this blind expectant mum was to turn up the volume on the heartbeat.
sentences.article_title: I never got to experience my baby's scan, but blind parents like me can now feel them

sentences.text: But now, parents like me can receive tactile 3D models created from their scans, allowing them to have a special moment with their unborn baby.
sentences.article_title: I never got to experience my baby's scan, but blind parents like me can now feel them

sentences.text: Reece Finnegan-Knight, who has been blind since his teens, is one of the first people to experience a 3D-printed model of his baby's scan with his wife, Sophy, as part of a new pilot scheme.
sentences.article_title: I never got to experience my baby's scan, but blind parents like me can now feel them

sentences.text: At their routine 12-week scan, Sophy had attempted to describe what she was seeing for Reece, but he struggled to feel involved in the moment.
sentences.article_title: I never got to experience my baby's scan, but blind parents like me can now feel them

sentences.text: Afterwards, when the couple showed the sonogram to their loved ones, Reece said it felt like "friends and family knew more about my baby than I did".

sentences.text: Professor Dave Chadwick from Bangor University sampling damaged remains following wildfires at Mynydd Llangynidr in Bannau Brycheiniog Scientists investigating the damage caused by severe wildfires across Wales this summer say the impact has been "catastrophic".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Extreme heat and exceptionally dry conditions throughout July and August left landscapes such as heathland, moorland and upland grasslands vulnerable to fast spreading fires, resulting in one of the UK's worst wildfire seasons in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones, who is leading a Bangor University survey of several sites across Wales, said the scale of damage was far greater than what was immediately visible.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "People see the blackened vegetation and assume that's the main impact, but the real story is below our feet," said Jones.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: During the July peak, fires affected approximately 2,760 acres of countryside across north Wales alone, the equivalent of more than 1,500 football pitches.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: At Sychnant Pass in Conwy county, one of the most significant blazes saw 36 homes having to be evacuated and about 200 acres of land affected.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones said the scale of damage from the wildfires was far greater than what was immediately visible At Sychnant Pass today, there are slight green shoots of recovery visible among the charred hillside.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: But Jones described a rare ecosystem housing specialist plants, butterflies and insects, "where the UK is the epicentre globally".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "We've probably lost about 10 centimetres of soil here [at Sychnant Pass] so we've lost all of that organic matter layer... 4,000 years of carbon gone in a single event," he said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Once the topsoil is gone, we can never recover that.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "People see the blackened vegetation and assume that's the main impact, but the real story is below our feet.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "This soil acts as a water sponge, a carbon store, a nutrient bank.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Losing it is a double whammy, it worsens climate change and makes the habitat far more fragile." He added: "This site has taken thousands of years to develop and it's all gone in maybe five days?
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "If we are going to try and put that soil back, generate artificial soils through the reuse of organic wastes for example, then it's important we understand what the soil quality is now.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "So that we can prepare for the future and design those soils, because they don't exist yet." Over recent weeks the Bangor team has been racing to collect soil samples at several sites across Wales before heavy winter rainfall washes away the remains.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Even NASA satellite data has been used to quickly identify new sites after fires have occurred.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Dr Kara Marsden says responding quickly is key Dr Kara Marsden, a lecturer in soil science who is also working on the project, said working at speed was vital.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "It was really important that we got on site very quickly to measure the soil and vegetation properties while the fire's impacts were still fresh," she said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "These things can change rapidly, so capturing that baseline data now means we'll have something accurate to compare against in future sampling dates." She warned that early green shoots now visible at the site did not necessarily reflect true or full recovery.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Bracken sprouts almost immediately because its rhizomes sit deep in the soil, so the burn layer wouldn't maybe have impacted those" she said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "But the heather and gorse have much shallower roots, so you know they're completely gone.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "They've been completely lost... that depth of soil they depend on could take thousands of years to form again." Jones said that the impact of such wildfires extended far beyond biodiversity loss.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Fires release carbon, nitrogen and sulphur back into the atmosphere, in itself contributing to climate change," he said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Every time we have a wildfire, we're just making the problem worse and worse.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "It becomes a self‑sustaining cycle... drier soils, more fires, more carbon released." He also warned that without rapid restoration and better wildfire preparedness, "we might lose pretty much all of this habitat within our lifetime".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: On Tuesday, Sony will release Marvel's Wolverine - the biggest game exclusive to the PlayStation 5 this year.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It's made by Insomniac, the studio responsible for the recent Spider-Man titles, which have sold 50 million copies in recent years.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: But unlike the friendly neighbourhood superhero, Wolverine has a Pegi-18 rating in the UK, meaning a child cannot legally buy the game, and it contains considerable levels of blood, gore and violence.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It represents a gamble for the studio responsible for some of Sony's biggest hits - will it turn out to have been worth it?
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: This review does not reveal the game's biggest moments, but beware minor spoilers for some of the characters that appear and a few early sequences.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Some of the images contain blood.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: The BBC’s Tom Gerken gets his claws on Marvel's Wolverine You play as Logan, aka Wolverine, the comic book superhero that can self-heal and has retractable claws.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Donning the famous yellow-and-black outfit (among others), you hack and slash your way through hordes of enemies.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: The combat is free-flowing and easy to pick up, as Wolverine stabs and slices his foes with copious amounts of blood on display.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Still, some may feel it doesn't go far enough.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Combat is built around a "rage" meter which fills as you take down enemies, with a full meter turning your surroundings grey and allowing you to swiftly dispatch your foes There are some stealth options, but I generally ignored them and went in with my claws out.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: The game didn't penalise me for this.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: You also unlock a slew of abilities, much like other games in the genre, meaning you get even more powerful as the game rumbles on.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And a clever system allows you to spend the rage you have accumulated to regenerate your health.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: The combat kept me hooked the whole way through the game, which took about 20 hours to get to the end credits.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: My colleague was faster, clocking in at about 15 hours.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It was so influential that it spawned a popular online gag, pointing fun at reviewers who couldn't help but repeat a cliché , external about the game making them feel like Spider-Man.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "There's a significant shake-up happening here in game design terms," freelance game critic Emma Kent told me.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Insomniac is moving away from Spider-Man's open world formula to adopt a linear structure for Wolverine.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "That means less open exploration, and a more curated path through the game world." The combat is broken up by short sequences where you explore high-detailed environments, which while fun at first began to drag as the game went on It adds to the gamble that comes with the game having such graphic violence.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Peter Parker and Miles Morales would go out of their way to avoid killing enemies - stringing them up or gluing them against walls with his webs - and there was no real gore to speak of," Kent said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Some games truly revel in showing detailed and over-exaggerated gore, but the violence in Marvel's Wolverine doesn't feel particularly gratuitous.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And the game's director Mike Daly accepted this came with a risk.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Even though this character appeals to kids, making a game that is explicitly like, 'sorry, this is not for kids, you should not play this game' - it does reduce the scope," he said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "But I think there was no other way to do it.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: That was the cost of doing business if we really wanted to set a game with this character in this universe." The graphics are great, but small cutscenes like this broke up the action too frequently for my taste One thing I didn't expect was the game's reliance on its performers.

sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Nonetheless, the acting is top drawer, with the standout being veteran performer Troy Baker (known for many roles including Joel in The Last of Us) who puts in a memorable performance as Nathaniel Essex.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Liam McIntyre, who plays Wolverine, told BBC Newsbeat he was "looking forward to people playing it".
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "I'm so proud that people are resonating with the story, with the performances, the character," he said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "This is such an astoundingly good character piece.

sentences.text: "I'm so happy that I've been able to make a Wolverine that hopefully people love." And to that point - when Hugh Jackman's famous take on the character last appeared on the big screen in 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine, it made $205m (then £160m) on opening weekend in the US - the best ever opening for an R-rated film.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It all suggests Sony's gamble may be a safer bet than it first seems.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Deadpool & Wolverine ultimately grossed $1.3bn worldwide at the box office,  suggesting there was a much bigger audience than expected for 18-rated violence The way you leap from building to building is superb, and feels excellent to control.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: But I'd rather there had been fewer acting sequences and more gameplay.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: On one or two occasions, in a cutscene Wolverine did something which felt like it broke a cardinal rule of game design to me - never show the player something cool when you could have let them do it themselves.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Still - the performances are of a high quality.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Troy and Liam in particular are performers where they get really invested in their characters and subject matter," Daly said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "They are part of the problem solving squad for who they are and how they bring that out - they brought a lot to the table.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Clearly the developers were inspired by narrative adventures like Uncharted for this kind of storytelling, and the gameplay even feels similar at times with chase and climbing sequences.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And while that game was genre-defining, it came out almost 20 years ago, so it's hardly a favourable comparison.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: In fact, perhaps the biggest issue for Wolverine is that it doesn't reinvent the wheel like Spider-Man did.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It's a game packed with tight combat and excellent performances, but it never threatens to meet the genre-defining heights of Insomniac's previous offering.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And Daly said there was a "monumental" amount of pressure that came with making the game following the success of Spider-Man - but as to whether the gamble paid off, he took a Zen view.

sentences.text: There was no alternative to developing AI, Anthropic boss Dario Amodei said The head of AI company Anthropic has called for the pace of development of artificial intelligence models to slow down and to be closely monitored.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Dario Amodei wrote in an online essay that developing AI was not in question, but that the risks associated with it were "serious" and that companies and governments must be given time to address them.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: The bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk, have both said they agree with Amodei.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: There have been growing concerns recently about the technology's potential risks.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: An AI researcher who left Anthropic told the BBC that "if we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Jacob Coxon told Laura Kuenssberg that people working at AI companies were "genuinely frightened... genuinely concerned about the fate of humanity in the next two years".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: "It's not at all an exaggeration to say that the people who are involved with both founding these companies and building the tech believe there is a possibility of human extinction," Coxon said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: In Amodei's essay, called We Must Pace the Frontier and published on Saturday, he proposed a three-point plan that included independent monitoring of AI models as they are developed, industry-wide regulation and global regulation.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: As his proposal made the rounds, even competitors voiced support for the idea of third-party monitors who could evaluate the safety of models as they are developed.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: "I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier," wrote OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on X.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: He called independent evaluators "a great idea".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'There is a possibility of human extinction,' former Anthropic employee says about AI Altman sounded similar safety concerns in a new interview, telling Fortune magazine that standards were "not at a place" to push AI capabilities much further.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: He added that he believed AI beyond human control was "absolutely" possible.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Musk, meanwhile, who founded Grok producer xAI, said the Anthropic boss was "right".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: The warnings have prompted calls to action, but US President Donald Trump has so far rejected such fears, saying on Thursday he was concerned that "if we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Cyber-security concerns have grown as new models have exhibited more and more powerful capabilities.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Anthropic withheld its Mythos model from public use when it was announced in April that it could independently escape the testing environment, known as the sandbox.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: In the run-up to the release of its most recent Astra model, OpenAI cited cyber-security concerns as it explained it had paused certain aspects of the model's development.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: The OpenAI agents had "essentially acted as a fanatically devoted collective", Amodei said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: OpenAI has said it was slowing down training of certain advanced AI models and tools as a result.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Safety has also taken centre stage in the rivalry between Anthropic and OpenAI.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Amodei, who had previously worked as a vice-president at OpenAI, has said he co-founded Anthropic in 2021 so he could build safer and more trusted AI models.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Amodei called for "building AI at a balanced rate that aims to ensure its safety while still achieving its benefits".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: This would not mean "halting model training or technical progress, but ensuring companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third party evaluators to confirm this".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: He was committing Anthropic to this "unilaterally" - as well as calling on governments "to require other frontier companies to match".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Amodei said he recognised that regulation might not be able to keep up with the pace of AI, and therefore called on AI companies to "voluntarily work together to set standard" in parallel with those regulation.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: The Anthropic CEO went on to address the impact that a slowdown would have on the industry and competition with leading developers worldwide, particularly China.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: "I believe that if slowing down bought us even an extra year or two before models reach critical levels of capability, and we used that time to advance alignment, we could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong," Amodei said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: This would have to be done in a co-ordinated manner "without sacrificing commercial advantage or the United States' lead in AI".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Any slowdown would have to be limited, he said, to avoid allowing China to pull ahead.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: He urged the US government to take measures so that US companies' AI chips could not be sold to China - or the technology shared with authoritarian countries.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: His former employee, Jacob Coxon, told the BBC, however, that the initiative to slow down must go beyond the US - "there'll need to be some sort of co-ordinated slowdown with China if we're going to avoid a race at an international scale".

sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: However, some observers suggested that Amodei's post was less about safety than about consolidating control over AI technology.

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Just last month, the European policing agency (Europol) had warned that museum thefts across Europe were growing increasingly brazen.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: And just days before the Renoir heist, internationally known art detective Arthur Brand predicted to the BBC that more high-profile burglaries were likely - particularly in the wake of the successful robbery at the Louvre in Paris last October .
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The audacious crime in one of the world's most famous museums stunned France, and the stolen jewellery worth €88m (£75m) has still not been recovered, nearly a year on.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We will see more of this," says Brand, "because if you are able to hit the Louvre, thieves all around the world are watching that, thinking, 'Wow' - and then they think, 'Don't we have a local museum with gold and silver?'".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: This video can not be played What we know about the Renoir museum heist Within hours of the Louvre burglary, thieves had raided coins from a smaller museum in France.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Since then, criminals have stolen a diamond necklace in Vienna , Bronze Age artefacts in Spain , and art from two Italian museums - and that's only what the BBC has written about.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The heist at the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer is the latest, and detectives are still working to track down the remaining multi-million-pound paintings - two of which were quickly recovered after thieves dropped them in the museum garden.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Europol tells the BBC the number of museum theft cases reported to them across Europe began to increase about two years ago.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Its recent report says both the methods and targets of thefts are changing - with a rise in more forceful tactics, and, as in the Louvre case, a focus on high-value items such as precious metals and gemstones.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Both Brand and Ibrahim Bulut, a museum security expert from a Belgian security consulting firm, believe many thefts that followed the Louvre burglary are copycats.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Every museum in the world is stressing now," Brand says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Data provided to the BBC by ARCA shows recorded museum thefts in France spiked in 2024, and rose again slightly in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, numbers go up and down over time, with more thefts recorded in 2015 than a decade later.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Others point out the colonial history behind many treasures in European museums, with art historians highlighting the French crown jewels stolen from the Louvre contained emeralds, diamonds, sapphires and pearls which are not native to France.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are vulnerable and easy to burgle, Brand says, compared with well-secured jewellery shops and banks - which these days hold less cash.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Directors historically "never have enough money for security" or prefer to spend it on the next exhibition, and museums are often housed in old buildings that are difficult to protect, he adds.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: For example, the Denis Diderot Maison des Lumières (House of Enlightenment) - burgled hours after the Louvre - is housed in two 18th-Century mansions in Langres.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We therefore have to reconcile modern security requirements with the need to preserve historic buildings and comply with France's heritage regulations," local mayor Théo Caviezel explains.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are also open public spaces that have less access control and perpetrators can come in as visitors, says Kumar Sokka, CEO of Acre Security which works with some museums in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: And even if a museum is secured well, thieves could still come in armed, Brand says, adding that it would be impractical to put police in galleries.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Many of these burglaries are over in minutes and the thieves have long gone by the time police show up - the Renoir case happened within five minutes.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Heists used to depend on deception, but burglaries are now becoming increasingly violent, Europol's report last month , external points out.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Offenders are using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars and, in some instances, explosives, to get inside.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In the Louvre, the thieves used a mechanical lift to gain access, cut through the window with power tools and then threatened guards, who left, before forcing their way inside displays and grabbing the jewels.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In the Renoir case, the perpetrators used an electric knife to cut through a fence before sawing through structures holding the paintings' frames in place.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The increased aggression creates new security concerns.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "An armed incident during opening hours, like the one we experienced, creates a situation in which the immediate priority is to keep our audience and staff safe," says Lilli Hollein, the director of the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK) in Vienna, which was burgled last month.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Two people leave Louvre in lift mounted to vehicle What is being stolen is also changing.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: While paintings are still taken, they're harder to sell, so about 10 years ago, thieves began shifting to goods that are easier to get rid of, Brand says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Now precious metals, gemstones, and culturally significant artefacts including Chinese porcelain are increasingly targeted, according to Europol's report.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Precious metals can be easily melted down, leaving no trace for law enforcement, and facilitating illicit sales during the fencing process," it says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Precious stones in jewellery, on the other hand, can be easily removed and sold further." Meanwhile, Chinese porcelain is likely to be easily sold on the art market because of high demand, Europol says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: After a theft, police generally have between four and six days to catch the thieves, according to Brand, who works with investigators by calling informants and receiving tips from the public or even ex-partners of perpetrators.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: But while suspects may be arrested, jewels or precious metals might not be found - such as with the Louvre case.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: On the other hand, Brand believes the Renoir paintings stolen this week - two of which were dropped by the thieves on their way out - "will probably be recovered" because "no one will want to buy" them and "it is likely, then, that the thieves have no idea what to do with them".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Christopher A Marinello, the boss of Art Recovery International that recovers stolen art, says only 5-10% of stolen art is ever recovered, making thefts from small museums like this week's "extra painful".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Tuesday's heist is another example of "Europe's museums under siege", he adds.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: After its theft in October, Maison des Lumières launched a security audit carried out by police officers appointed by France's cultural ministry, mayor Caviezel says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Some recommendations are already being implemented, such as enhanced video surveillance, while other structural improvements are in the process of being developed.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: MAK in Vienna also increased its security to prevent "copycat offenders and to provide our audience with visible security", its director says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Entry is through a metal detector, and bags must be put in the cloakroom or in lockers, and there are more security guards.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Experts say the trick is to create physical barriers that will delay thieves so there is time for the police to arrive, or to make any theft take so long that it would deter would-be offenders from attempting it.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Security is about buying time", says Bulut.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Sokka says it's critical to have integrated systems - so for example if an alarm goes off, you could shut down the facility, or lock down all high net worth paintings.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, security measures are expensive.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Mayor Caviezel, whose small French city hosts two museums and collections, says finding the money is "one of our main challenges".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "A small city can be entrusted with collections of national importance without having the financial resources of a major Parisian institution." Bulut, who sits on the International Committee for Museum Security board, says it's not all about expensive gadgets.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: It could also be training guards to spot suspicious people who may be casing a museum and ask them if they need help, which may deter them from returning.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are investing: Sokka says his company has seen an uptick in seismic offerings, that can detect vibration such as drilling in walls, in the past 18 months.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museum heists are not increasing everywhere in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In Sweden, major museum thefts began to decline around a decade ago and have not changed significantly in recent years, said Peg Magnusson, Sweden's representative for a Unesco convention to combat illicit trafficking of cultural property.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, other worrying cultural artefact targets have emerged.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The challenge for museums now is increasing security while also staying open to the public.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "A museum cannot be a fortress," Hollein says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We want to be open institutions; at the same time, we are facing new challenges and attacks against museums that will require new standards." Additional reporting by Madeleine Lake.
